data.name: Amam
data.gender_notes: Amam is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A title given to Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) wife Aisha (ra). The name Amam carries the meaning “Mother of Mothers” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Pashto. Parents who choose Amam usually hope their child will grow to embody mother of mothers and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of unconditional love and nurturing
data.etymology: Amam belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mother of Mothers.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amam total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_arabic.name: أمام
in_arabic.meaning: أمام يعني الشخص الذي يأتي في المقدمة أو يقود الجماعة
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم أمام مشتق من الجذر العربي 'أم' و 'م' ويدل على القيادة والإمامة في الدين الإسلامي. يشير إلى الشخص الذي يأتي في المقدمة أو يقود الجماعة في الصلاة أو في الحياة اليومية. ورد ذكره في القرآن الكريم في سياق الإمامة والقيادة.

in_urdu.name: امام
in_urdu.meaning: امام کا مطلب ہے وہ شخص جو نماز کی قیادت کرتا ہے یا کسی جماعت کا رہنما ہوتا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: امام نام عربی جڑوں سے نکلا ہے اور اسلامی روایت میں اہم کردار رکھتا ہے۔ یہ نام ان شخصیتوں کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو نماز کی قیادت کرتے ہیں یا کسی اسلامی جماعت کی رہنمائی کرتے ہیں۔ اس کا ذکر قرآن کریم میں امام کی ذمہ داریوں اور صفات کے حوالے سے کیا گیا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: इमाम
in_hindi.meaning: इमाम का अर्थ है वह व्यक्ति जो नमाज़ का नेतृत्व करता है या किसी समुदाय का मार्गदर्शक होता है
in_hindi.long_meaning: इमाम नाम की उत्पत्ति अरबी भाषा से हुई है और यह इस्लामी परंपरा में महत्वपूर्ण स्थान रखता है। यह नाम उन व्यक्तियों के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है जो नमाज़ का नेतृत्व करते हैं या किसी इस्लामी समुदाय का मार्गदर्शन करते हैं। इसका उल्लेख कुरआन में इमाम की जिम्मेदारियों और गुणों के संबंध में किया गया है।

in_pashto.name: امام
in_pashto.meaning: امام دى هغه څوک چې د لمونځ مشري کوي يا د يوه ټولنې مشر وي
in_pashto.long_meaning: امام نوم د عربي ريښو څخه اخستل شوي دي او په اسلامي روايت کې مهم رول لري. دا نوم د هغو کسانو لپاره کارول کېږي چې د لمونځ مشري کوي يا د يوه اسلامي ټولنې مشري کوي. دا په قرآن کريم کې د امام د مسئوليتونو او صفاتو په اړه ذکر شوي دي.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Amina" has historical significance in Islamic culture as it was the name of Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) beloved wife, Aisha bint Abu Bakr (ra), who was known for her intelligence, beauty, and piety. She is considered a role model for Muslim women and plays a significant role in Islamic history.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Aisha" holds deep spiritual significance as she was not only a beloved wife of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) but also his devoted companion and teacher. She is known to have spent a considerable amount of time learning and memorizing the Quran from the Prophet. Aisha's contributions to Islam through her scholarship, piety, and wisdom continue to inspire and guide Muslims to this day. The name "Aisha" is symbolic of the Prophet's deep connection with his wives and the profound impact they had on the development and teaching of Islam.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Mother of Mothers" symbolizes A title given to Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) wife Aisha (ra). In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Amam serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of mother of mothers.

historical_references.reference: Amam ibn al-Mundhir was the last ruler of the Rashidun Caliphate, which marked the first era of Islamic political history. He ruled from 656-661 CE during a period of instability and civil war after the death of Caliph Ali. Amam was declared caliph by the army and was known for his military campaigns against the Byzantines and Sasanians. His reign was marked by internal power struggles and external military engagements, and he was eventually assassinated during a rebellion.
historical_references.context: First Islamic Political History, Rashidun Caliphate, Military Campaigns, Power Struggles, Assassination

historical_references.reference: Amam ibn Yasir is recorded in Islamic history as one of the early converts to Islam, and is known as the 'First Martyr of Islam'. He embraced Islam during the early years of the Prophet Muhammad's mission in Mecca, around 615 CE. He was a wealthy merchant and a close companion of Abu Bakr, the first caliph of Islam. When the persecution of Muslims in Mecca became too severe, Amam and his family emigrated to Medina, joining the Muslim community there. Shortly after their arrival, Amam and his family were martyred in a raid by the Meccan army.
historical_references.context: Early Islamic History, First Muslim Martyr, Emigration to Medina, Persecution in Mecca
